title: Canonical coherent tensor structure on a fixed normalized precomposition core
statement: For arbitrary small sites, let p be an InternalPrecompositionMorphism with identity structural ring map and core an InternalModulePullback p satisfying InternalModulePullbackLaws [def-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor-data]. Then there exists P : InternalExactTensorPullback p whose core equals the supplied core. Thus only the canonical comparison, section pure-tensor equation, and symmetric monoidal coherence are constructed; scalar-extension objects, module adjunction, multiplication unitor, section identifications, and exactness are inputs and remain identical.

source.place: Tags 03D7, 03CY, 03DA and Section 03EK; internal-action application of steps 1--6 of lem-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor.

proof.text: The geometric inverse image preserves finite products and is a left adjoint. The balanced-tensor universal property and module sheafification therefore construct the canonical inverse-image tensor comparison. Identity scalar extension and core.unitor transport it to the specified pullback. Its generalized pure-tensor normalization is insertion of 1; the multiplication equations in InternalModulePullbackLaws reduce this insertion to the identity.

source.place: Tags 03D7, 03CY, 03DA and Section 03EK; internal-action application of steps 1--6 of lem-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor.

proof.text: Precomposition and the section-identification equation in the laws evaluate the comparison to the identity on the presheaf pure tensors. The regular ring gives the unit map, which becomes the identity after multiplication. Bilinear uniqueness proves naturality, symmetry and the two unit equations. Trilinear uniqueness proves associativity because both composites send (x tensor y) tensor z to x tensor (y tensor z). These laws define a Monoidal structure with μ the inverse of the recorded comparison.

proof.text: Package the input core and its laws with the comparison, pure-tensor equation and coherence data just constructed. The resulting core is definitionally the original core.
